channel.title: The E-Wrestling Museum: new accessions
channel.description: The newest accessions of the e-wrestling museum, each a lot numbered in the order it arrived.

item.title: Accession 0304: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of the UWF's own site, uwfonline.com, by the url-walk: the pages of its news desk and rumor column, its front page, its general information page, a show preview and its wrestler profile pages. It stands behind 35 pages of the UWF wing.

item.title: Accession 0303: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of six pages of Primetime Central's own 2003 site (ptc.wrestleonline.org): its February 2003 headlines (the sale of PTC to two long-time members and the move of its forums), its Ads page of recruitment notices, the February 2003 edition of its rules with the four federation tiers, its top ten and ratings lists of 4 April, and the World Wrestling Alliance's channel profile. It stands behind five pages of the PTC and WWA wings.

item.title: Accession 0302: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of pages of the eWrestling Network's own site, ewnweb.net and ewnweb.com, that the donated backup of the same site (lot 0170) does not hold: one post of the hub's CuteNews desk (24 April 2005), the EWNWeb.net news page of 10 February 2003 (an iteration earlier than the backup's), and four news posts of RUSH Pro Wrestling's own site, which www.ewnweb.com carried in August 2004. It stands behind 6 pages of the EWN and RPW wings.

item.title: Accession 0301: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of five more pages of PCW's own site that the donated database of lot 0159 does not carry: the move lists and roster cards of two wrestlers, Skitzo and Agent Matt Jackson, captured between February and June 2003, and the front page of October 2003 with the owner's farewell. It stands behind five pages of the PCW wing.

item.title: Accession 0300: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of twelve pages the content census of 11 October 2026 found unserved in three small fed sites: the Underground Brawler's Club's Jurisdiction card page and its singles and tag team application forms, Global Championship Wrestling's application form, its LiveWire X2 board index and six wrestlers' roleplay topics from its GCW Studios forum, and TRAUMA:fighting's message board index. It stands behind twelve pages of the UBC, GCW and tF wings.

item.title: Accession 0299: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of the Canadian Heat Zone's own 2002 site, whose September 2002 pages the donated database of lot 0159 holds: the June to August editions of its news, rumors, front, champions, roster and application pages, its headline columns of June and August, and the roster cards of fourteen of its wrestlers. It stands behind twenty-two pages of the CHZ wing and its tag team Dick on a Stick.

item.title: Accession 0298: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of one topic of The Quill, a general creative-writing board on rpcommunity.com: "No More Tears", Jay Phoenix's first-person backstory roleplay, posted on 28 June 2004 by the handle Phoenix, with the two replies the topic shows. It stands behind one roleplay on the 4WW wing.

item.title: Accession 0296: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of five pages of PCW's own site that the donated database of lot 0159 does not carry in full: the results of Sunday Adrenaline of 19 January 2003, and the closing parts of four roleplays of May and June 2003 whose first parts the donated database holds. It stands behind the Sunday Adrenaline card; the four roleplays stay documents of lot 0159, each naming its capture as a second source.

item.title: Accession 0295: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of eVolution's own site, which the donated database of lot 0159 also covers: its Tainted Love 2004 transcript, the Legends of 7 April 2004, the news items that report its shut-down, the 2005 edition of its history page, and the site's own biographies, career histories and timeline stories of its wrestlers. It stands behind the last cards, the closing news and the history of the eVolution wing, and behind thirteen character pages.

item.title: Accession 0294: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of PRIME's own site, prime.theewe.net, that the donated database of lot 0159 does not hold: the full show reviews of ReVolution 34 (Charlotte, 9 June 2004), ReVolution 49 (Sacramento, 1 December 2004) and ReVolution 50 (Edmonton, 15 December 2004, the fiftieth edition). It stands behind three cards of the PRIME wing, the oldest served PRIME shows.

item.title: Accession 0293: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of three federations' own sites that the donated database of lot 0159 also covers: PRIME's ReVolution cards of 22 June and 5 July 2005 and its 2005 application page, PWC's sixteen scripted television commercials and its card for 21 June 2003, and PURE's Ikusa results of 2 February 2003, its card preview and three newswire items. It stands behind the cards, commercials and news pages of the PRIME, PWC and PURE wings.

item.title: Accession 0292: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: Two small e-feds read from their own sites: the New Revolution Wrestling League, a blog-format fed whose page runs to May 2014, and High Caliber Championship Wrestling, a Tumblr e-fed of about 2018, each taken as the one front page it posted.

item.title: Accession 0291: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: Wayback recoveries of the pages of the Championship International Wrestling Alliance, a free simulation interfed on Expage in 2001, and of its member feds TCW, FSW and CWA: the alliance's home page and FAQ, four home pages, three rosters, a results page and a pay-per-view card, read as the news, rules, rosters and results each posted about itself.

item.title: Accession 0290: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: Six small e-fed message boards read in place: Project: Honor (2020), Full Metal Wrestling (to 2014), the French Association Mondiale de Catch (2020), Eagle Eye Wrestling (2011), the Dynamite Wrestling Alliance (2018) and the French Grind Pro Wrestling (2021), each topic taken whole from its own page: character sheets, cards, results, promos and announcements.

item.title: Accession 0289: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: Three small e-feds read from their own sites: the American Wrestling Alliance (awawrestling.net, 1999 to 2008), Extreme Madness Wrestling (a fantasy fed that meant to become a CAW league, 2009 to 2011) and the Apex Wrestling Syndicate (2014 to 2015), taken as the news, staff, rules, card, awards and hall-of-fame pages each posted about itself.

item.title: Accession 0288: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: Wayback recoveries of the home pages of three small e-feds: Strike Fantasy Towers (SFT) of 2003, the Universal Wrestling Circuit of 2005 to 2006, and Legends Championship Wrestling of 2005 to 2009, read as the menus, champion panels, news and results each posted about itself.

item.title: Accession 0287: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: Wayback recoveries of the home pages of four small e-feds, TWC (Takeley Wrestling Championships) of 2004 to 2005, Imaginary Championship Wrestling of 2006 to 2008, NWA-TNA of 2004 to 2008 and the Global Wrestling Organisation of 2001, and the news page of All Star Wrestling Inc., parent of the All Star Wrestling Alliance, of 2001, read as the news, menus, top lists and announcements each posted about itself.

item.title: Accession 0286: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The Yahoo Wrestling Association's own Spanish-language board, 2010 to 2015, read where the promotion wrote it: weekly AWZ cards and results, pay-per-view reports and the general manager's announcements.

item.title: Accession 0285: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: Wayback recoveries of the home pages of three small e-feds: American Championship Wrestling's Bravehost site (2006 to 2007), All Star Wrestling on GeoCities (2001 to 2009) and Fantasy Creatures Wrestling (2003), read as the champions, cards, news and staff each fed posted about itself.

item.title: Accession 0284: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: Wayback recoveries of the front pages of three small e-feds: American Wrestling Federations (2005 to 2010), Extreme Wrestling Entertainment's ProBoards board (2005 to 2007) and Alpha Championship Wrestling (2004 to 2006), read as the champions, rankings, cards, staff and news each fed posted about itself.

item.title: Accession 0283: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of New True Internet Championship Wrestling's own site, nticw.homestead.com, captured from February to November 2001: the weekly-show federation whose handlers filled in a profile card for each wrestler, read as the cards, show scripts, columns, rules and title pages it published itself. It stands behind the NTICW (2000) wing's profile documents.

item.title: Accession 0282: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of Primetime Championship Wrestling's own site on its primetimewrestling.net address, captured from August 2001 to January 2003: the fed's wrestler biographies posted in November 2001 and a set of character histories from the autumn of 2002. It stands behind the PCW wing's biography and history documents of those dates.

item.title: Accession 0281: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of the Atlantic Wrestling Club's own site on its two addresses (awc.supremepixels.net and awc.supremepixels.com), captured from April 2005 to September 2007, read for what the federation's backstage database does not hold. It stands behind the AWC wing's front pages, rosters, announcement page, a wrestler's original card and the earliest roleplay on the site.

item.title: Accession 0280: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of the IIeW organizer's own site on the Carleton University free-net (ncf.carleton.ca), captured from August 1997 to January 2001: the pages of the International Invitationals of e-Wrestling (the 28 February and 1 March 1998 supercard, the Deschenes Cup tournaments), the organizer's own wrestler, "Playboy" Ronnie D, and the text of two of that wrestler's EMWC matches of April 1998. It stands behind the IIeW wing's site pages and two EMWC match scripts served in the EMWC wing.

item.title: Accession 0279: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of the address epic.slike.com, captured from November 2001 to December 2004, holding Epic Wrestling's own site: the angle-based federation of 2001 and 2002 where Sean Simon Williams' Hardcore Isosceles Trapezoid held the North American Championship, read as the biography cards, shows, site pages, title histories and fan-board posts it published itself.

item.title: Accession 0278: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of the Championship Wrestling League's own site, www.thecwl.com, captured from March to August 2001: the league Ed Wilson owned, read as the front page, help pages, biographies, title histories, news, shows, chapters and columns it published itself.

item.title: Accession 0277: Private donation
item.description: Eighteen pieces from the promoter's own e-mail archive: the UWF's closing, its farewell show cards and its 2006 announcements, two Gary Clark pieces of 2005, a Viking Terror application, GCW's 2006 and 2010 notices, three 2012 applications and segments for Internet Championship Wrestling, and the RingHype tournaments announcement.

item.title: Accession 0276: Private donation · Contributed by the Janitor
item.description: Four pieces from the promoter's own e-mail archive: three February 2011 applications to the UiWF (Johnny Legend, WHOA and Jamie Shock) and the Phenomenons' June 2014 zoo-liberation promo for NAPW, handed over as forwarded mail rather than found on the public web.

item.title: Accession 0275: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of further World Wrestling Alliance pages: the 2016 wrestler bio pages and 2010 webcast scripts of wwa-online.com, the 2005 and 2006 wrestler pages and pay-per-view archive of wwa-online.net, and 2001 and 2002 pages of wwa-wrestling.org.

item.title: Accession 0274: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of Cyberspace Championship Wrestling's own sites: the Angelfire pages of 1999 to 2001, theccw.com of 2001 and theccw.net of 2002, read as the daily show scripts, the 2002 roleplay directory, the roster and bio cards, the title and champion pages, the news and the standing pages the fed published itself.

item.title: Accession 0273: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The World's Finest Wrestling (WFW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, November 2004 to January 2005: the broadcasts of Guerra Interminable, Ghoulish Games and the first nine parts of Christmas Card, the promos for them, the presidential campaign and Felix Red's election, the new characters' profiles of December and January, and the fed's own history of the BAD World Heavyweight Title.

item.title: Accession 0272: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The jOlt league's boards on the fwrestling.com hub, July 2012 to October 2015: the fed's announcements of its shows from the spring of 2013 to its final show, its in-story news of 2013 to 2015 (a death, a suspension, the company going public and falling short), its recruiting notices and a returning writer's story.

item.title: Accession 0271: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The World's Finest Wrestling (WFW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, August to October 2004: the broadcasts of Cherry Blossom Chaos II and Paradise Lost, the promos for them and for Guerra Interminable, the Inner Circle's arrival, the presidential primaries, and the character profiles of the fed's roster that the founder reposted in October.

item.title: Accession 0270: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The jOlt league's boards on the fwrestling.com hub, July 2011 to February 2013: the staff's recruiting and welcome notices, the members' reviews of the revived jOlt's first shows (iNtense 35 to Warriors 8 and Divide & Conquer), polls between its characters and the returning writers' own accounts of the company.

item.title: Accession 0269: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The NGEN (New Generation Enterprises) boards on the fwrestling.com hub, January 2010 to January 2011: its founder's announcements and welcome post, the wrestler profiles of the new roster, the roleplay folders and the broadcast parts of the first pay-per-view, Cherry Blossom Chaos, and his notes on writing it.

item.title: Accession 0268: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: A Wayback recovery of jOlt Wrestling's own sites: jolt.slike.com (November 2001 to June 2002, its first two seasons) and www.joltwrestling.com (February to March 2005, its third), read as the shows, standing pages, roster cards, news and information pages the fed published itself.

item.title: Accession 0267: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The World's Finest Wrestling (WFW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, April to July 2004: the broadcasts of the Superbowl of Wrestling, Shock & Awe II, BOMB Voyage and WWF Pandamonium, the War Games of Vox Hiberionacum Part Deux, the promos for them and for Cherry Blossom Chaos, the presidential campaign and election, and character profiles of the new roster.

item.title: Accession 0266: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The World's Finest Wrestling (WFW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, January to March 2004: the end of the Merrython broadcast, the broadcasts of Mind Over Matter, Great Expectations, Road to Glory (the So Cal Rumble) and the first half of Vox Hiberionacum Part Deux, the promos for them, the Superbowl of Wrestling line-up and the commissioner's profiles of past characters of the early Fantasy Wrestling leagues.

item.title: Accession 0265: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The Great Lakes Championship Wrestling (GLCW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, July to November 2003: Columbus Riptide, Akron Wired, Wisconsin Dells Riptide, Joliet Wired and half of the last Riptide, the match-folder roleplays, the president's announcement that the fed was closing and the members' farewells.

item.title: Accession 0264: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The World's Finest Wrestling (WFW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, October to December 2003: the broadcast posts of New World Madness, Ghoulish Games, Turkey Day Terror and Merrython, the promos for their matches, the first President's messages and the new wrestlers' profiles.

item.title: Accession 0263: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The Great Lakes Championship Wrestling (GLCW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, March to June 2003: the Green Bay house show, Milwaukee Riptide, Flint Wired, Indianapolis Riptide, the Duluth show and Ringlords I, the fed's first pay-per-view, with the card lineups, the match-folder roleplays, the second Brutal Truth, a roll call of the members and the president's rule on the title's name.

item.title: Accession 0262: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The Great Lakes Championship Wrestling (GLCW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, December 2002 to February 2003: the rest of the Rockford Riptide broadcast, the Toledo, Saginaw and Hammond house shows, Kalamazoo Riptide, Massive Assault 2002 and Cleveland Riptide, the card lineups, the match-folder roleplays, the first Brutal Truth and the president's updated roster.

item.title: Accession 0261: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The World's Finest Wrestling (WFW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, July to September 2003: the promos and broadcast posts of Scars and Stripes Forever, Paradise Lost, Spirit of NGEN, NYC Unplugged and Almost Live, the 2003 election of the league's first President, and the new wrestlers' profiles.

item.title: Accession 0260: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The World's Finest Wrestling (WFW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, January to June 2003: the league's welcome and rules, the lineups, the match-folder roleplays and the show posts of the Curt Hennig Memorial Show, Almost Live, Vox Hiberionacum, Shock & Awe, Gates of Hell, Cherry Blossom Chaos and Rage in the Cage, and the first wrestler profiles.

item.title: Accession 0259: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The New Frontier Wrestling (NFW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, July 2014 to March 2020, from RELOADED 21 and the Texas Two-Step tour to the fed's last posts: the films forum's fan videos and scripts, the president's billed line-ups and the members' feedback on the posted cards, the status thread through the fed's long pause, and the farewell thread; with a BRAWL 55 roleplay thread, a board discussion and a filled character application from 2007 to 2013 that the hub's forum index left undated.

item.title: Accession 0258: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The New Frontier Wrestling (NFW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, February 2013 to June 2014, from BRAWLHALLA and RELOADED 15 to BRAWL 72 and RELOADED 21: the president's notes and the members' feedback on each posted card, the setlist and roll-call threads, the roleplay threads of the Brute 66 tour, the Random Rumble and the films forum, and the press conferences.

item.title: Accession 0257: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The New Frontier Wrestling (NFW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, October 2011 to January 2013, from BRAWL Hampton and RELOADED X to RELOADED 14: the show posts and the members' reviews, the setlist and matchwriting sign-ups, the BRAWLAPALOOZA and BRAWLFERENDUM threads, the Ask NFW sticky and four roleplays.

item.title: Accession 0256: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The Great Lakes Championship Wrestling (GLCW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, June to November 2002: the president's application, rules and mission statement, the members' filled applications, the card lineups, the match-folder roleplays and the show posts of First Wave, Riptide, Racine Riptide, Chi-Town Showdown I, South Bend Riptide and the house shows.

item.title: Accession 0255: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The New Frontier Wrestling (NFW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, December 2010 to September 2011, from the winter meetings to Reloaded in Raleigh: the Brawl, Reloaded and SUPERCRASH 3 show posts and the members' reviews, the matchwriting assignments and progress notes, the sign-up and deadline notes, the Hall of Fame page, the Grand Prix threads and five roleplays.

item.title: Accession 0254: Web-recovery campaign
item.description: The New Frontier Wrestling (NFW) forum on the fwrestling.com hub, June 2009 to October 2010, from Crash 49 and the long road to Crash 50 to the BRAWL and RELOADED house-show tours: the Crash 49 and Crash 50 lineup, matchwriting and roleplay threads, the Impulse roleplays, the WAYstation and signed-matches threads, the post-Crash 50 roll call and the character applications.
